blocks.html: This project brings together everything from Chapters 4 to 10 in one menu-driven C++ program that a real school office could use. It stores student records, generates report cards, prepares a merit list and shows class statistics.

items.html: Apply decomposition (Chapter 4) to break a real problem into functions
Use structures, vectors and maps together (Chapters 9 and 10)
Practise input validation, loops, switch menus and formatted output (Chapters 5 and 6)
Write reusable functions with call by reference and const references (Chapter 7)
Use string input with getline() (Chapter 8)

rows: Reads roll number, name and marks in 5 subjects; rejects duplicate roll numbers and marks outside 0–100
Prints a formatted table of all records
Prints a full report card for one roll number, marking weak subjects
Changes marks in one subject and recalculates total, percentage and grade
Removes a record by roll number
Shows all students ranked by percentage (highest first)
Class average, topper, pass percentage, subject averages and a star chart of grades

blocks.html: Grading rule used: A (90+), B (75–89.99), C (60–74.99), D (33–59.99), F (below 33).

findIndex()

items.html: Save the code as result_system.cpp .
Compile: g++ result_system.cpp -o result_system (or press Build and Run in
Run: ./result_system (Linux/macOS) or result_system.exe (Windows).
Choose options from the menu. Add at least 5 students to test the merit list and
Subject-wise pass rule: Mark the result as "Compartment" if the student scores below 33 in any one subject, even if the overall percentage is above 33.
Search by name: Add an option to find students whose name contains a given word (use find() from Chapter 8).
Section-wise data: Use map<string, vector<Student>> with sections "A", "B", "C" as keys.
Binary search: Keep the vector sorted by roll number and search with binary search (Chapter 9).
Attendance: Add an attendance percentage member; show a warning below 75%.
Save to file: Store records in a text file so they are not lost when the program closes (file handling is covered in Class 12).
